_comment: 30 synthetic security alerts for routing. ground_truth in {enterprise, email, cloud, review}. 'review' = genuinely insufficient/ambiguous context, where escalation is the correct answer. 'scenario' tags the three cases walked through on stage. See data/SCHEMA.md.

alerts.text: CrowdStrike Falcon: process injection on WKS-2290 (user jdoe). mimikatz.exe spawned from powershell.exe with an LSASS memory read attempt. Host quarantined.
Microsoft Defender quarantined an Emotet variant on SRV-FS03. A scheduled task was created for persistence under C:\Windows\Temp\svc.exe.
Host IDS: SMB lateral movement from 10.12.4.33 to 11 internal hosts over port 445 within 90 seconds. Pass-the-hash pattern suspected.
EDR: unsigned binary 'svch0st.exe' executing from %APPDATA% on LAPTOP-FIN12 and beaconing every 60s to a known C2 IP (45.9.148.x).
On-prem Active Directory: 240 failed Kerberos pre-auth attempts against the DOMAIN\svc-backup account in 2 minutes, all sourced from workstation HR-114.
Sysmon: credential-dumping tool wrote to disk on DEV-BUILD-07; parent process cmd.exe launched by a service account outside its baseline working hours.
Antivirus console: ransomware canary files modified on file server SRV-NAS01, with a rapid sequential-encryption pattern spreading across the \\finance share.
Host firewall on WKS-5521 repeatedly blocked outbound connections to a Tor entry node every ~5 minutes since 02:00 local.
User-reported phishing: message from 'payroll@adp-secure[.]com', subject 'Updated Direct Deposit', with an HTML attachment 'form.html' that renders a fake Microsoft 365 login to harvest credentials.
Proofpoint flagged an inbound message carrying a password-protected archive 'invoice_8831.zip' containing a Qakbot loader. Delivered to 14 mailboxes before the block.
Business email compromise: a CEO-impersonation email requesting an urgent wire transfer, with reply-to set to an external gmail.com address. Display name matches the real CEO.
Secure email gateway blocked a campaign of 320 messages from the lookalike domain 'rnicrosoft[.]com' containing a credential-phishing link.
User clicked a link in an email that led to a fake DocuSign login page and submitted their corporate credentials before reporting it.
Spam filter: a spoofed internal sender 'it-helpdesk@' is asking users to 'verify mailbox quota' through an external link. ~40 recipients.
Attachment sandbox detonation: 'Resume_2026.doc' with a macro that downloads a second-stage payload. Sender is an external recruiter domain.
A phishing campaign is being sent from a compromised internal Microsoft 365 account (user mchen), which is now blasting lookalike-invoice emails to the entire finance distribution list.
GuardDuty: anomalous IAM API calls — CreateAccessKey followed by AttachUserPolicy (AdministratorAccess) — for the 'ci-deploy' user from a new IP in eu-west-1.
S3 bucket 'acme-customer-pii' ACL was changed to public-read; roughly 1.2M objects are now world-readable.
Okta: impossible-travel sign-in for user asingh — London then Lagos within 8 minutes — with MFA satisfied via push on both.
Azure AD: three new OAuth app consent grants requesting Mail.Read and Files.ReadWrite.All across the tenant, approved by non-admin users within an hour.
CloudTrail: GetSecretValue calls from a Lambda execution role spiked ~400x above baseline, pulling secrets the function has never read before.
GCP: a service-account key was created and immediately used from an unrecognized ASN to enumerate every storage bucket in project prod-data.
Entra ID: a legacy-auth (IMAP) sign-in succeeded for an executive account from a foreign IP, bypassing the tenant's conditional-access policy.
AWS: a root-account console login from an unfamiliar device, with no MFA challenge recorded in CloudTrail for the session.
Alert: anomalous activity detected on asset HOST-4471. Risk score 72. No additional detail available from the connector.
SIEM correlation rule 'Suspicious Behavior - Multiple' triggered for user kpatel. 3 sub-events referenced; details truncated at the log forwarder.
Raw syslog flagged by the anomaly model, no classification: '<134>Oct 03 02:14:51 fw01 %ASA-6-302013: Built inbound TCP connection 889 for outside'.
Threat-intel feed reports a match on IOC 185.220.101.4 observed 'somewhere in the environment'; the originating source system is not identified in the alert.
User-submitted ticket: 'I think I got hacked?? something weird happened on my computer and also my email looked off.' No artifacts, logs, or host details attached.
DLP alert: 'sensitive data movement detected'. Destination and channel fields are null; the connector integration is reporting a degraded state.
